claim: Genetic variation at the MTIF3 locus has been robustly associated with obesity in humans.
source: Genetic variation at the MTIF3 (Mitochondrial Translational Initiation Factor 3) locus has been robustly associated with obesity in humans, but the functional basis behind this association is not known.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature establishing the association between MTIF3 genetic variation and obesity.

claim: The rs67785913-centered DNA fragment (in LD with rs1885988, r2 > 0.8) enhances transcription in a luciferase reporter assay.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from luciferase reporter assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9-edited rs67785913 CTCT cells show significantly higher MTIF3 expression than rs67785913 CT cells.

claim: Perturbed MTIF3 expression led to reduced mitochondrial respiration.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Seahorse mitochondrial respiration assays.

claim: Perturbed MTIF3 expression led to reduced endogenous fatty acid oxidation.

claim: Perturbed MTIF3 expression led to altered expression of mitochondrial DNA-encoded genes and proteins.

claim: Perturbed MTIF3 expression led to disturbed mitochondrial OXPHOS complex assembly.

claim: Excessive weight gain caused by dietary excess can cause life-threatening disease.
source: Excessive weight gain caused by dietary excess, and its effects on adipocyte lipid metabolism, can cause life-threatening disease (Appleton et al., 2013; Denis and Obin, 2013; Chu et al., 2017; Lotta et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The effects of excessive weight gain on adipocyte lipid metabolism can cause life-threatening disease.
source: Excessive weight gain caused by dietary excess, and its effects on adipocyte lipid metabolism, can cause life-threatening disease (Appleton et al., 2013; Denis and Obin, 2013; Chu et al., 2017; Lotta et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Findings from clinical trials showed the MTIF3 variation modulates weight loss-promoting exposures on body weight.
source: Findings from clinical trials (Papandonatos et al., 2015), a bariatric surgery case series (Rasmussen-Torvik et al., 2015) and epidemiological cohorts (Nettleton et al., 2015) showed the MTIF3 variation modulates weight loss-promoting exposures on body weight (see also UK Biobank analysis in Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The MTIF3 rs1885988 C allele correlates with higher MTIF3 expression in subcutaneous fat tissue.
source: Here, we validated MTIF3 rs1885988 C allele correlates with higher MTIF3 expression in subcutaneous fat tissue
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental validation of GTEx data.

claim: The tightly linked rs67785913 variant is likely to be the actual eQTL for MTIF3 expression.
source: and our in vitro luciferase reporter assay and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing results revealed that the tightly linked rs67785913 variant is likely to be the actual eQTL for MTIF3 expression (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from luciferase assays and CRISPR-Cas9 editing.

claim: Pre-adipocyte cell lines have been used extensively for studying adipogenic differentiation.
source: Pre-adipocyte cell lines have been used extensively for studying adipogenic differentiation (Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The application of pre-adipocyte cell lines for lipid metabolism studies has been limited, especially in the context of gene–environment interaction.
source: but their application for lipid metabolism studies has been limited, especially in the context of gene–environment interaction.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: Variation of differentiation capacity across cell passages can alter baseline phenotypes in differentiated cells.
source: This is largely due to the variation of differentiation capacity across cell passages (Poulos et al., 2010) and differential genetic effects on adipocyte differentiation (Kamble et al., 2020), which can alter baseline phenotypes in differentiated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Differential genetic effects on adipocyte differentiation can alter baseline phenotypes in differentiated cells.
source: This is largely due to the variation of differentiation capacity across cell passages (Poulos et al., 2010) and differential genetic effects on adipocyte differentiation (Kamble et al., 2020), which can alter baseline phenotypes in differentiated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MTIF3 deficiency results in lower content of mitochondrial DNA-encoding proteins in adipocytes.
source: Our data show that in adipocytes MTIF3 deficiency results in lower content of mitochondrial DNA-encoding proteins and altered expression of several mitochondrial DNA-encoding genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from western blotting and qPCR.

claim: MTIF3 deficiency results in altered expression of several mitochondrial DNA-encoding genes in adipocytes.
source: Our data show that in adipocytes MTIF3 deficiency results in lower content of mitochondrial DNA-encoding proteins and altered expression of several mitochondrial DNA-encoding genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from qPCR.

claim: MTIF3 deficiency leads to disassembly of mitochondrial respiration OXPHOS complex in adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, it leads to disassembly of mitochondrial respiration OXPHOS complex, along with impaired mitochondrial respiration rate (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: MTIF3 deficiency leads to impaired mitochondrial respiration rate in adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, it leads to disassembly of mitochondrial respiration OXPHOS complex, along with impaired mitochondrial respiration rate (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: MTIF3 vastly affects the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that MTIF3 vastly affects the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from multiple experimental results.

claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction in white adipose tissue has been frequently associated with obesity.
source: Mitochondrial dysfunction in white adipose tissue has been frequently associated with obesity (Kaaman et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The presumed mechanisms of mitochondrial dysfunction association with obesity are decreased fatty acid oxidation and ATP production.
source: with the presumed mechanisms being decreased fatty acid oxidation and ATP production (reviewed in Heinonen et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: One causal link connecting mitochondrial dysfunction and obesity may be the MTIF3 content.
source: We have found that one causal link connecting these factors may be the MTIF3 content (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: A previous study described an inverse relationship between mitochondrial capacity and weight change.
source: Furthermore, a previous study described an inverse relationship between mitochondrial capacity and weight change (Jokinen et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Any genetic variation-modulated change in MTIF3 expression could influence a dietary intervention outcome.
source: thus, conceivably, any genetic variation-modulated change in MTIF3 expression could influence a dietary intervention outcome.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior studies and current findings.

claim: MTIF3-deficient adipocytes exposed to glucose restriction challenge responded less through changed triglyceride content.
source: We found that MTIF3-deficient adipocytes exposed to glucose restriction challenge responded less through changed triglyceride content, indicating limited capacity for lipid metabolism under glucose restriction (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: MTIF3-deficient adipocytes have limited capacity for lipid metabolism under glucose restriction.
source: We found that MTIF3-deficient adipocytes exposed to glucose restriction challenge responded less through changed triglyceride content, indicating limited capacity for lipid metabolism under glucose restriction (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: MTIF3 knockouts, having reduced fatty acid oxidation, re-esterify the released fatty acids to triglycerides, and thus retain more triglycerides during glucose restriction.
source: Here, we speculate that MTIF3 knockouts, having reduced fatty acid oxidation, re-esterify the released fatty acids to triglycerides, and thus retain more triglycerides during glucose restriction.
evidence: This claim is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: Mitochondrial function is robustly associated with insulin sensitivity.
source: Mitochondrial function is robustly associated with insulin sensitivity (Böhm et al., 2020; Pietiläinen et al., 2008; Heinonen et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Both mitochondrial function and insulin sensitivity can be improved through lifestyle intervention aiming at weight loss.
source: both of which can be improved through lifestyle intervention aiming at weight loss (Phielix et al., 2010; Toledo et al., 2007; Larson-Meyer et al., 2006; Civitarese et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Impaired adipocyte differentiation derived from mitochondrial dysfunction in adipose tissue often associates with insulin resistance in humans and animal models.
source: Furthermore, impaired adipocyte differentiation derived from mitochondrial dysfunction in adipose tissue often associates with insulin resistance in humans and animal models (Sakers et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: We did not observe impaired adipocyte differentiation due to MTIF3 deficiency or rs67785913 eQTL.
source: In our study, we did not observe impaired adipocyte differentiation due to MTIF3 deficiency or rs67785913 eQTL.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from adipogenic marker measurements.

claim: The lower content of glycolysis intermediates and odd-chain fatty acids in MTIF3 knockout adipocytes could indicate blunted lipogenesis.
source: The lower content of glycolysis intermediates and odd-chain fatty acids in MTIF3 knockout adipocytes could indicate blunted lipogenesis
evidence: This claim is based on inference from metabolomics data.

claim: The decreased essential and non-essential amino acid level in MTIF3 knockout cells under glucose restriction could be an adaption to the lower energy supply owing to impaired mitochondrial function.
source: while the decreased essential and non-essential amino acid level in MTIF3 knockout cells under glucose restriction could be an adaption to the lower energy supply owing to impaired mitochondrial function (Hansson et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from metabolomics data and citation to prior literature.

claim: MTIF3 plays a vital role in triglyceride metabolism in adipocytes.
source: The metabolite data, and the earlier described lower fatty acid oxidation capacity of MTIF3-deficient cells, suggest that MTIF3 plays a vital role in triglyceride metabolism in adipocytes
evidence: This claim is based on inference from metabolomics and fatty acid oxidation data.

claim: The common genetic variant rs67785913 is a functional polymorphism that causes modulated MTIF3 expression.
source: In summary, we experimentally demonstrated that the common genetic variant rs67785913 is a functional polymorphism that causes modulated MTIF3 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from luciferase assays and CRISPR-Cas9 editing.

claim: MTIF3 is essential for mitochondrial electron transport chain complex assembly in human adipocyte cell lines.
source: Our functional genomics studies demonstrate that MTIF3 is essential for mitochondrial electron transport chain complex assembly, mitochondrial function, and lipid metabolism in human adipocyte cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Blue Native-PAGE and other assays.

claim: MTIF3 is essential for mitochondrial function in human adipocyte cell lines.
source: Our functional genomics studies demonstrate that MTIF3 is essential for mitochondrial electron transport chain complex assembly, mitochondrial function, and lipid metabolism in human adipocyte cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Seahorse assays.

claim: MTIF3 is essential for lipid metabolism in human adipocyte cell lines.
source: Our functional genomics studies demonstrate that MTIF3 is essential for mitochondrial electron transport chain complex assembly, mitochondrial function, and lipid metabolism in human adipocyte cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fatty acid oxidation and triglyceride content assays.

claim: MTIF3 content may influence adipocyte triglyceride content in conditions that mimic dietary restriction, reflecting a gene x environment interaction.
source: MTIF3 content may also influence adipocyte triglyceride content in conditions that mimic dietary restriction, reflecting a gene x environment interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from glucose restriction experiments.

claim: Higher MTIF3 content in adipocytes increases mitochondrial function.
source: Since our findings show that higher MTIF3 content in adipocytes increases mitochondrial function, this helps explain the previously observed interaction between MTIF3 locus and weight loss interventions.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from experimental data showing reduced mitochondrial function in MTIF3 knockout cells.

claim: Higher MTIF3 content in adipocytes helps explain the previously observed interaction between MTIF3 locus and weight loss interventions.
source: Since our findings show that higher MTIF3 content in adipocytes increases mitochondrial function, this helps explain the previously observed interaction between MTIF3 locus and weight loss interventions.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from current findings and prior literature.

claim: People who carry genetic variants that increase MTIF3 expression (e.g., the rs67785913 CTCT allele) may benefit more from lifestyle interventions targeting weight loss.
source: Furthermore, this suggests, although it remains to be demonstrated, that people who carry genetic variants that increase MTIF3 expression (e.g., the rs67785913 CTCT allele) may benefit more from lifestyle interventions targeting weight loss.
evidence: This claim is explicitly stated as speculation that remains to be demonstrated.

claim: A human white pre-adipocyte cell line (hWAs) was previously isolated and immortalized from human subcutaneous white adipose tissue of a female subject, aged 56 with a BMI of 30.8.
source: A human white pre-adipocyte cell line (hWAs) was previously isolated and immortalized from human subcutaneous white adipose tissue of a female subject, aged 56 with a BMI of 30.8. The generation and characterization of hWAs were described previously (Xue et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature describing the cell line.

claim: MTIF3 is a mitochondrial translation initiation factor.
source: MTIF3 is a mitochondrial translation initiation factor; thus, we examined the effects of MTIF3 ablation on differentiated hWAs adipocyte mitochondrial respiration chain.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about MTIF3 function.

claim: MTIF3 has a role previously ascribed to it in OXPHOS complex assembly.
source: Next, we hypothesized the above observations could have originated from the insufficient MTIF3 supply during OXPHOS complex assembly (a role previously ascribed to MTIF3 [Rudler et al., 2019]).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature (Rudler et al., 2019).

claim: MTIF3 facilitates initiation complex formation on mitochondrial 55S ribosomes in the presence of MTIF2, fMet-tRNA, and poly(A,U,G).
source: The post-transcriptional rate-limiting translation step can be promoted by MTIF3, as it facilitates initiation complex formation on mitochondrial 55S ribosomes in the presence of MTIF2, fMet-tRNA, and poly(A,U,G) (Bhargava and Spremulli, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature (Bhargava and Spremulli, 2005).
